item.title: Documentary | Shenzhen: Beyond the Skyline
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Shenzhen, the host city of APEC 2026, is in many ways the embodiment of China's development miracle. But its story goes far beyond the skyline. From mangrove wetlands to bustling electronics markets, from contemporary art to everyday life in a care home, Xinhua's Miao Xiaojuan explores the people and ideas shaping this metropolis, and what it means to live well here. item.title: Xi congratulates new members of BiH Presidency on taking office
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
BEIJING, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday congratulated Zeljka Cvijanovic, Denis Becirovic and Darijana Filipovic on their assuming office as members of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH). Noting that BiH is an important partner of China in Southeast Europe, Xi said that in recent years, bilateral relations have maintained steady and healthy development, political mutual trust has grown increasingly strong, and fruitful cooperation has been achieved in various fields. Xi said he attaches great importance to the development of China-BiH relations and stands ready to work with the members of the Presidency to deepen the traditional friendship and mutually beneficial cooperation between the two countries, steer bilateral ties to a higher level, and bring greater benefits to the peoples of both countries. ■

item.title: Policy synergy supports China's steady growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- China's economy maintained overall stability in October, with new growth drivers strengthening and the economic structure improving, as enhanced policy coordination helped underpin solid growth, official data showed on Monday. The National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) said the value-added industrial output of enterprises rose 4.8 percent year on year in October, while the service production index increased 4.6 percent last month. The surveyed urban unemployment rate stood at 5.1 percent, down 0.1 percentage point from September, and the consumer price index rose 0.7 percent year on year. In the January-October period, retail sales of goods and services, a major indicator of the country's consumption strength, expanded 2.5 percent year on year, with service retail sales up 4.9 percent. China's goods imports and exports totaled 44.81 trillion yuan (about 6.67 trillion U.S. dollars), surging by 20 percent. China's fixed-asset investment, meanwhile, dropped 8.1 percent year on year in the first 10 months of 2026. Excluding the property sector, the country's fixed-asset investment decreased by 5.1 percent in the first 10 months of the year. Investment in intellectual property products rose 9.2 percent, pointing to a shift toward innovation-driven growth. The steady momentum came as China strengthened coordination of existing and incremental policies, channeling resources into innovation, industrial upgrading and new quality productive forces. As a result, high-tech manufacturing value-added jumped 17.6 percent in October, and equipment manufacturing value-added grew 10.6 percent. Production of 3D-printing equipment, lithium-ion batteries and industrial robots surged 85.9 percent, 30 percent and 26 percent, respectively, while new energy vehicle output rose 17.1 percent. NBS spokesperson Fu Linghui said the economy maintained overall stability in October and continued the momentum of "new driving forces and improved structure." New growth drivers, represented by high-end and smart manufacturing, contributed more than half of the growth in industrial value-added in the first 10 months of 2026. Foreign trade was a bright spot. China's goods imports and exports in October climbed 31.2 percent year on year to 4.87 trillion yuan, with exports up 28.7 percent and imports increasing by 34.7 percent. In the January-October period, trade with Belt and Road partner countries increased 18.5 percent, trade by private enterprises rose 20.1 percent, and exports of mechanical and electrical products grew by 25.2 percent. Exports of high-tech products and that of the "new three," namely photovoltaic products, lithium-ion batteries and electric vehicles, all soared by more than 50 percent in October, Fu said. "The seamless transition between new and traditional growth drivers is the result of our persistent and steady efforts over many years to promote high-quality development," noted Wang Guanhua, another NBS spokesperson. "It is something we have long anticipated and hoped for, and it will provide stronger support for the economy going forward." However, Fu cautioned that the international environment remains unstable and uncertain, the imbalance between supply and demand at home is still prominent, and some enterprises face operational difficulties. The foundation for steady economic improvement still needs to be consolidated, he explained. "Next, efforts should be made to ensure the effective implementation of policies, further unleash domestic demand potential, optimize supply, deepen reform and opening up, enhance development momentum and vitality, and improve people's livelihoods," Fu added. China's gross domestic product grew 4.6 percent year on year in the first three quarters of 2026, and the October data suggested that this steady performance remained intact despite domestic and external headwinds, according to Wang. Wang said coordinated macro policies will help the economy continue its innovation-driven, high-quality and improved development, providing support and conditions for achieving the full-year growth target. China is targeting economic growth of 4.5 percent to 5 percent in 2026 and will strive for better in practice, this year's government work report noted. ■

item.title: China's APEC moment: Xi's vision for an open, inclusive Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
SHENZHEN, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- For decades, the Asia-Pacific has been one of the most important engines of global economic growth. Yet as globalization faces mounting headwinds, the region is confronting a fundamental question: can openness and cooperation, the very source of its success, continue to power its future? Against this backdrop, leaders of APEC member economies will gather in Shenzhen, a city at the forefront of China's opening up, to chart a course for the region's future. Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. He has consistently championed deeper regional economic integration, greater openness and connectivity as part of his broader vision of building an Asia-Pacific community. "We should stay true to APEC's founding mission to promote economic growth and improve people's lives, and champion open development where everyone shares opportunities and emerges a winner," Xi said at last year's APEC meeting in the Republic of Korea (ROK). IDEAS SHAPING A CLOSER COMMUNITY Founded in 1989, APEC now brings together 21 member economies, including China, Russia and the United States. China joined in 1991. The forum has helped expand trade and investment and strengthen economic ties across the Asia-Pacific. Together, these economies account for nearly 40 percent of the world's population, more than 60 percent of global GDP and nearly half of world trade. Over the past three decades, per capita income across the region has more than quadrupled, while more than one billion people have been lifted out of poverty. Behind this progress has been a sustained commitment to regional cooperation. Since 2013, Xi has put forward ideas and proposals through the APEC platform on how economies with diverse interests and development priorities can work together and shape the region's future. At the 2013 APEC CEO Summit in Bali, Indonesia, Xi called for a strong sense of community of common destiny in the Asia-Pacific, advocating common development, open development, innovation-driven development and interconnected growth. "The Asia-Pacific economies are interdependent on each other, with shared interests and common destiny. The success or failure of one may ultimately lead to success or failure of all," he said. The idea was further developed in the years that followed. In 2014, when China hosted APEC in Beijing, Xi advocated an Asia-Pacific partnership featuring mutual trust, inclusiveness, cooperation and win-win results. That year, members launched the process toward a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) and endorsed the APEC Connectivity Blueprint, giving fresh impetus to regional economic integration. In 2020, APEC members adopted the Putrajaya Vision 2040, setting a goal of building an open, dynamic, resilient and peaceful Asia-Pacific community. Xi described the vision as a new starting point for the next phase of regional cooperation, calling for a community with a shared future built on openness and inclusiveness, innovation-driven growth, greater connectivity and mutually beneficial cooperation. At the 2025 meeting in Gyeongju, the ROK, Xi put forward five proposals on safeguarding the multilateral trading system, fostering an open regional economy, keeping industrial and supply chains stable and smooth, advancing digital and green trade, and promoting universally beneficial and inclusive development. Together, the proposals gave concrete shape to the idea of an Asia-Pacific community. As China hosts APEC this year, its vision for Asia-Pacific cooperation remains rooted in Xi's concept of a community with a shared future for humanity, with shared prosperity as a common goal. OPENNESS, INNOVATION, COOPERATION China identified openness, innovation and cooperation as the priorities for its APEC chairmanship, seeking to inject fresh momentum into Asia-Pacific development. Openness has long been central to APEC's pursuit of regional growth and prosperity. As Xi noted in Gyeongju last year, APEC was founded in response to economic globalization, with the goal of promoting trade and investment liberalization and facilitation and supporting economic growth and prosperity. Over the years, openness has lowered barriers to trade and investment, deepening economic integration across the region through a growing network of trade arrangements and cooperation mechanisms. The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) is now fully in force among its members, with tariffs on more than 90 percent of goods traded among them eventually set to be eliminated. China is also working to align with high-standard international economic and trade rules, including those embodied in the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) and the Digital Economy Partnership Agreement. Last year, China and ASEAN signed the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol. Greater openness has gone hand in hand with stronger connectivity, with railways, ports and other infrastructure helping deepen economic links and improve trade routes across the region. The Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, the China-Laos Railway and Peru's Chancay Port are among the projects driving this closer connectivity. Innovation is opening up new sources of growth. As Xi said at the APEC CEO Summit in Vietnam in 2017, "To avoid the risk of the global economy entering a 'new mediocre,' we must sustain growth through innovation." Areas such as digitalization and green transformation are creating new opportunities for the Asia-Pacific to overcome traditional growth constraints and tap new areas of cooperation. APEC economies have embraced the digital transformation, with internet penetration rising from 52 percent to nearly 90 percent over the past 12 years. The region's green transition is also gaining momentum. Electric vehicles accounted for 25.5 percent of total motor vehicle sales in APEC economies in 2024, up from 7.4 percent in 2018. About 22 million EVs were sold across the region in 2024. The benefits of innovation can also be seen in concrete projects across the region. Chinese enterprises are supporting the development of new-energy vehicle industries in Thailand, green technologies are helping transform urban transport in Chile, and Juncao technology has helped farmers in Fiji increase their incomes. Such cooperation demonstrates how technology and innovation can be turned into practical solutions for sustainable development. Innovation creates new opportunities, while cooperation helps build community. The theme for APEC 2026, "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," reflects China's longstanding commitment to pursuing win-win outcomes with its Asia-Pacific partners. China has translated this vision into concrete action. It has granted zero-tariff treatment covering 100 percent of tariff lines to all least developed countries that have diplomatic relations with China. "True development is development for all," Xi said in San Francisco in 2023. He urged members to "develop greater synergy in our development strategies and work together to resolve the global development deficit," highlighting cooperation as a pathway to more inclusive growth and a stronger sense of community across the region. FUTURE OF ASIA-PACIFIC China's APEC chairmanship has brought extensive engagement across the region, with more than 300 meetings and events held this year. These have included senior officials' meetings, ministerial meetings covering areas from trade and tourism to energy, transportation and finance, as well as high-level events under APEC Digital Weeks. The focus now shifts to Shenzhen, where leaders of APEC economies will consider priorities for the next phase of regional cooperation. The meeting comes at a time when protectionism and geopolitical tensions are testing regional economic ties, while advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and other technologies are creating new opportunities for growth. Advancing regional economic integration will remain a central priority at the Shenzhen meeting. Twenty years after the FTAAP vision was put forward, leaders are expected to consider ways to advance the vision, including through closer coordination among existing trade agreements such as the RCEP and CPTPP. They are also expected to look at strengthening regional connectivity, building on the APEC Connectivity Blueprint for 2015-2025. AI will be another major focus, as APEC economies seek to turn rapid advances in digital and intelligent technologies into new sources of growth. Discussions are likely to cover how to harness these technologies for growth while building broader common ground on their development and governance. China has advanced that agenda during its chairmanship. At the APEC Digital and AI Ministerial Meeting in Chengdu, Sichuan, in July, open-source development was highlighted at the APEC ministerial level for the first time, alongside recognition of the importance of intellectual property protection. China has also advanced practical cooperation through new regional platforms. It has announced plans for a center for APEC cooperation on cross-border data flows in Qianhai, Shenzhen, and launched initiatives to establish an Asia-Pacific cooperation center for AI empowerment of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Guangzhou and an Asia-Pacific SME Cooperation Zone in Shenzhen. As China advances its modernization drive, it will continue to deepen reform and expand high-standard opening up, creating new opportunities for the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. As Xi put it at the APEC CEO Summit in Lima in 2024, "China's development is inseparable from the Asia-Pacific, and it will in turn further benefit the region." ■

item.title: Xinhua Commentary: APEC Shenzhen meeting to inject fresh momentum into Asia-Pacific cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
SHENZHEN, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Asia-Pacific cooperation now stands at a crossroads amid mounting economic uncertainty and rising protectionism. The upcoming 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting offers a timely opportunity to reaffirm the region's commitment to openness and cooperation, and inject much-needed certainty and fresh momentum into regional and global growth. The Nov. 18-19 meeting in Shenzhen, south China, is expected to lay the main pillars of an Asia-Pacific community, coordinate different pathways toward the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, make new arrangements to boost regional connectivity, and advance digital, smart and green transformation for the region to prosper together. Against the backdrop of a sluggish global economy, there could be no better occasion than the Shenzhen meeting to send a resounding message of championing free trade, deepening regional economic integration, opposing protectionism and "decoupling," and enhancing the resilience of industrial and supply chains. Interactions among leaders of APEC economies are also expected to help enhance mutual trust and build consensus -- a positive signal for global peace and development. The 2026 APEC "China Year" has seen more than 300 meetings and activities held across Chinese cities, laying a solid foundation for fruitful outcomes during the Shenzhen meeting. The meeting is expected to adopt an APEC leaders' declaration, with practical outcomes in key areas such as trade, connectivity, the digital economy and artificial intelligence (AI). Business leaders from across the region and beyond will also gather in Shenzhen for the APEC CEO Summit, where cooperation in AI, the digital economy and green development will be high on the agenda and is expected to create new drivers of growth for the Asia-Pacific economy. The prosperity of the Asia-Pacific over the past few decades has been built on open cooperation and industrial complementarity, rather than bloc confrontation and economic fragmentation. This is the underlying logic behind the region's remarkable growth and its role as a major engine of the world economy. Over the years, China has played a leading role in advancing Asia-Pacific cooperation, offering ideas and solutions to promote common development. Meanwhile, China-proposed international public goods, such as the Belt and Road Initiative, have remarkably boosted economic and trade cooperation in the region. China will remain committed to promoting high-standard opening up, and continuously provide new opportunities for shared growth via its modernization drive. Its super-large market, booming AI, digital economy, green technologies and wider opening up will unlock new potential of cooperation in the region. APEC serves as both an incubator of ideas and a platform for building consensus and advancing cooperation. In today's complex and volatile world, the value of its flexible, pragmatic and results-oriented approach is clearer than ever. China's leader has urged staying true to APEC's founding mission to promote economic growth and improve people's lives, and championing open development where everyone shares opportunities and emerges a winner. As leaders of APEC member economies gather in Shenzhen, a coastal city at the forefront of China's opening up and innovation drive, they have an opportunity to demonstrate that openness, inclusiveness and mutually beneficial cooperation remain the foundations of regional prosperity. The Shenzhen meeting is set to help build an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together, and chart an open, innovative and cooperative future for the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. ■

item.title: Full text
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
MANILA, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday delivered a speech at the 29th China-ASEAN Summit. The following is the full text of the speech: Remarks by H.E. Li Qiang Premier of the State Council of the People's Republic of China At the 29th China-ASEAN Summit Manila, November 16, 2026 Dear Colleagues, It is my great pleasure to join you at this meeting. This year marks the fifth anniversary of the China-ASEAN Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. Over the past five years, we have witnessed a growing countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism and recurring geopolitical conflicts on the global stage. Despite such a challenging environment, China-ASEAN cooperation has maintained strong momentum and scored encouraging achievements. First, we have elevated our cooperation in both output and quality. Trade between the two sides exceeded US$1 trillion last year, up by 20.1 percent compared with 2021. In the first 10 months of this year, our trade increased by 29.6 percent. To date, two-way investment has exceeded US$500 billion in cumulative terms, an increase of over 50 percent compared with five years ago. Cooperation in new areas such as digital economy, green economy and artificial intelligence has made rapid advances. Second, we have further consolidated cooperation mechanisms. We signed the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, creating the institutional foundation for building a mega-sized regional market. We also adopted and delivered on the Plan of Action to Implement the ASEAN-China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (2026-2030), drawing a promising blueprint for common development in the next five years. Third, we have continued to strengthen connectivity. Major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung high-speed railway and the China-Laos railway were turned from plans into reality, the Pinglu Canal was officially opened, and the "ASEAN Visa" program was implemented. The flow of personnel, capital, technology and other factors has become more efficient across the region, and generated greater economic returns. The past five years have been truly extraordinary, and the achievements we scored have not come easily. From our shared journey, we can draw some valuable experience and inspirations, particularly the following three points. First, promoting the tradition of friendship and mutual assistance. China and ASEAN countries share a long history of friendly exchanges. Instead of losing its shine in the turbulent world, this fine tradition has grown more mature and resilient as we work together to tackle one challenge after another. Second, upholding the fundamental principles of openness and mutual benefit. China and ASEAN are both long-standing advocates and contributors of economic globalization and regional integration. Although economic and trade restrictions have substantially increased around the world, we remain firmly committed to safeguarding multilateralism and promoting free trade, and endeavor to make the pie of cooperation bigger. Third, embracing the trend of innovation-driven development. Amid rapid advances in science and technology, we have kept abreast of the times, and worked together to strengthen innovation capabilities and open up new vistas for economic growth. These experience and inspirations are a valuable asset for us all. We must carry them forward and harness them to the fullest so as to keep writing new chapters of China-ASEAN cooperation. Colleagues, Five years ago, President Xi Jinping put forward the vision of China and ASEAN jointly building a peaceful, safe and secure, prosperous, beautiful and amicable home. China and ASEAN countries both value the concept of family. We enjoy geographical proximity and our people feel close to each other. Our profound friendship, which has been nurtured over generations, shall not and will not be swayed by any temporary or isolated issue. As we now live in a volatile world, it is all the more important for China and ASEAN to stand united and remove disruptions. We should jointly build an even closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future, preserve and build our home well, and provide greater stability and certainty for the development and prosperity of the entire global village. First, we should strengthen the safeguards for peace and tranquility. The more complex and severe the international landscape is, the more imperative it is for us to build up strategic trust, properly handle differences through dialogue and negotiation, jointly oppose foreign interference, and uphold regional peace and stability. China looks forward to the early adoption of a Code of Conduct in the South China Sea, so as to provide solid institutional safeguards for lasting peace and stability in the South China Sea. Second, we should promote regional development and prosperity. We should take the entry into force of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol as an opportunity to deepen industrial and supply chain cooperation, accelerate the development of "hard connectivity" of infrastructure including railways and highways, and strengthen "soft connectivity" in areas such as mechanisms, standards and rules. China welcomes the establishment of the China-ASEAN energy cooperation partnership and the mechanism of energy ministerial meeting. China will work with ASEAN to host a successful Year of AI Cooperation in the next year, carry out "AI plus" cooperation, and explore the alignment with the ASEAN's Digital Economy Framework Agreement, so as to cultivate powerful engines for the high-quality development of the regional economy. Third, we should increase the benefits to the people. Making life better for the people is an important task for all of us. China will continue to replenish the China-ASEAN Cooperation Fund, and stands ready to step up cooperation with ASEAN on poverty reduction, disaster prevention and mitigation and food security to promote sustainable development of the region. The China-ASEAN Digital Academy will provide 100 full scholarships for ASEAN countries next year and the China-ASEAN Women and Children's Health Cooperation Center is ready to work with ASEAN countries to train 1,000 professionals in the coming three years. We welcome your active participation in these programs. China is willing to strengthen law enforcement cooperation with ASEAN to jointly combat transnational crimes and ensure people's safety. When the family is in harmony, everything thrives; when people are in harmony, everything goes well. I believe that with the close collaboration between our two sides, our shared home will stay vibrant and prosperous, and embrace a brighter future. Thank you. ■

item.title: Chinese premier urges China, ASEAN to stand united, overcome distractions
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Chinese Premier Li Qiang attends the 29th China-ASEAN Summit in Manila, the Philippines, Nov. 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) MANILA, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Monday that in a turbulent and complex world, China and ASEAN should stand united, overcome distractions and work together to build a closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future. Li made the remarks during the 29th China-ASEAN Summit in Manila. As this year marks the fifth anniversary of the establishment of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, Li said that over the past five years, the world has witnessed a growing trend of unilateralism and protectionism, while geopolitical conflicts have flared up one after another. Against this backdrop, China-ASEAN cooperation has forged ahead, achieving both quantitative growth and qualitative improvements, with cooperation mechanisms further consolidated and connectivity steadily enhanced, he said. The extraordinary five years and the hard-won achievements offer valuable experience and useful lessons, Li said. He stressed that both sides need to carry forward their tradition of friendship and mutual assistance, uphold the right path of openness and win-win cooperation, and keep pace with the trend of innovation and development. These experiences and lessons are a valuable asset shared by both sides and should be upheld and put to full use over the long term, Li said. Five years ago, Chinese President Xi Jinping proposed that China and ASEAN work together to build a peaceful, safe and secure, prosperous, beautiful and amicable home, Li said, adding that both China and ASEAN countries cherish the culture of family and are geographically close and bound by strong people-to-people ties. The profound bonds forged over generations should not, and will not, be affected by temporary events or circumstances, he said. Li urged China and ASEAN countries to protect and develop their common home, injecting greater stability and certainty into the development and prosperity of the global village. He called on the two sides to strengthen the foundations for peace and security by properly handling differences through dialogue and consultation, jointly opposing external interference, and safeguarding regional peace and stability. China looks forward to the early conclusion of the Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea, which will provide a solid institutional guarantee for lasting peace and stability in the South China Sea, Li said. He also called for promoting regional development and prosperity, stressing the need for both sides to take the entry into force of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area (FTA) 3.0 Upgrade Protocol as an opportunity to deepen industrial and supply chain cooperation, accelerate infrastructure connectivity, or "hard connectivity," in areas such as railways and highways, and strengthen "soft connectivity" in mechanisms, standards and rules. The premier said China applauds the establishment of a China-ASEAN mechanism for energy ministers' meetings and stands ready to work with ASEAN to successfully hold the China-ASEAN Year of artificial intelligence (AI) cooperation next year, advance "AI+" cooperation and create a strong engine for high-quality regional economic development. Li also called for improving the well-being of the people, voicing China's readiness to continue to contribute to the China-ASEAN Cooperation Fund and strengthen cooperation with ASEAN in areas including poverty reduction, disaster prevention and mitigation, food security, maternal and child health, so as to promote sustainable development in the region. Commending the fruitful outcomes achieved over the five years since the establishment of the ASEAN-China comprehensive strategic partnership, leaders of ASEAN countries expressed readiness to strengthen strategic communication and political mutual trust with China, fully implement the ASEAN-China FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, and deepen cooperation in areas including economy and trade, connectivity, AI, clean energy, digital economy and combating transnational crime. They thanked China for its consistent support for ASEAN centrality in the regional architecture and its commitment to the peaceful settlement of disputes. They also expressed the hope for an early conclusion of the COC in the South China Sea, jointly safeguarding regional peace and stability, and building an ASEAN-China community with a shared future. It was announced during the meeting that the China-ASEAN FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol will enter into force on Dec. 1, 2026, and 2027 has been designated as the Year of AI cooperation. Outcome documents were released, covering the 5th anniversary of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, energy partnership building, and deeper forestry cooperation. ■ Chinese Premier Li Qiang attends the 29th China-ASEAN Summit in Manila, the Philippines, Nov. 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Ling)

item.title: Xi congratulates Jinan University on its 120th founding anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday sent a congratulatory letter to Jinan University, celebrating its 120th founding anniversary. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, extended congratulations to the faculty, students and alumni of the university. Xi urged the university to carry forward its patriotic traditions and distinctive educational features, and to foster more young talent among compatriots in Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan and overseas Chinese. He also called on the university to carry forward and promote Chinese culture and advance friendly exchanges between China and the world. The university was asked to improve its education and teaching quality and make new contributions to pooling strength among overseas Chinese and advancing Chinese modernization. Founded in 1906, the university in south China's Guangdong Province has, over the past 120 years, nurtured a wealth of outstanding talent for Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, as well as for more than 170 countries. ■

item.title: Xi urges breaking new ground in high-quality development of Greater Bay Area
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, visits an artificial island of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a sea-crossing project connecting the cities of Shenzhen, Zhongshan and Guangzhou, in south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 16, 2026. Xi made an inspection tour on Monday in Zhongshan, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) ZHONGSHAN, Guangdong, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday urged efforts to thoroughly study and implement the guiding principles of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, and to strive to break new ground in the high-quality development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection tour in Zhongshan, south China's Guangdong Province. Stressing fully and faithfully implementing the decisions and arrangements made at the plenary session and leveraging new progress in persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, Xi urged a better job in advancing integrated development along the Pearl River Estuary. Visiting an artificial island of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a sea-crossing project connecting the cities of Shenzhen, Zhongshan and Guangzhou, Xi demanded efforts to further enhance the management and operation of this mega transport project to better serve the development of the Greater Bay Area. At an industrial park in Zhongshan, Xi learned about local efforts to absorb industrial transfers, transform and upgrade traditional industries, and develop emerging industries. Building the Greater Bay Area is a major strategic plan made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi said, calling on cities along the Pearl River Estuary including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Dongguan and Zhongshan to play a pioneering role. Xi expressed the hope that Zhongshan would seize the opportunities, take reform and innovation as the fundamental driving force, improve regional cooperation mechanisms, foster a sound business environment, and vigorously promote the deep integration of technological innovation and industrial innovation. Speaking to representatives of small and medium-sized enterprises and sci-tech personnel, Xi encouraged them to make greater contributions to the development of Guangdong and the Greater Bay Area and China's greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology. Xi also visited the Museum of Dr. Sun Yat-sen and laid a floral basket before his bronze statue. This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. On the new journey, it is necessary to emulate, inherit and promote his invaluable spirit, and inspire all Chinese people at home and abroad to unite and strive to build a great country and advance national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization, Xi said.
